sections.html:
The fastest way out is generally an as-is cash sale. Listing the house means open houses, an appraisal and a buyer who still has to clear a lender. Boca Raton has older single-family streets and plenty of condominiums, so the best path depends on the property type and on what a building association requires of you.

  • Cash buyer: few contingencies, and you agree on the closing day together.
  • Agent listing: wider exposure, plus repair requests and lender deadlines.
  • Owner sale: the contract and the closing agent are your job.

Whichever you pick, collect the parcel record, loan payoff letters and permit history before a buyer calls. One folder with all three shortens most deals.

Only one other city in Palm Beach County is larger than Boca Raton. More than 75 percent of its housing was built after 1970, and the median single-family price climbed from $268,000 in 2000 to $502,272 in 2019. The city counted 91,797 permanent residents in 2017 and projects 101,652 full-time and seasonal residents by 2040, so ask your agent or buyer how the winter season affects timing.

Code enforcement handles housing standards, and the city plans systematic inspections in areas with older structures. Older houses with historic standing are covered by the Historic Preservation Ordinance. Call the city before planning rehab work or a teardown.

  • The Community Appearance Board enforces upkeep standards, mostly on commercial and industrial property.
  • Periodic bulk trash pickups make it easier to clear a house before listing.
  • The city helps owners of historically significant housing apply for state and federal assistance programs.

For open permits, ask the city's Planning, Zoning and Building staff. The county appraiser does not keep permit or situs address records, so a buyer's agent will be sent to the city for those.

sections.h2: How the county values your home
sections.html:
The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser sets three numbers for each parcel. Just value is market value. Assessed value is just value less caps such as Save Our Homes. Taxable value is assessed value less exemptions, and it is the figure the tax collector bills.

Each value is struck as of January 1. Staff look at every property at least once in five years, in person or from aerial photos. Each parcel page has a tax calculator where a buyer can enter a purchase price and say whether they will homestead, which lets them estimate their own bill before making an offer.

Property appraiser rules that matter at a sale
TopicWhat applies
Homestead filing deadlineMarch 1
Homestead assessed increase cap3 percent a year
Non-homestead cap10 percent a year
After a saleExemptions removed and value reset to market on the next January 1
ExemptionsMove with the owner, not with the property

sections.h2: Your homestead exemption when you sell
sections.html:
The exemption is yours, so it travels to your next home. The buyer has to file for their own. If you sell during the year, it can stay on the property until the next January 1, but it is no longer working for the new owner.

With portability, your Save Our Homes savings can follow you to a new Florida homestead. You have three tax years to port after losing a homestead. The portability form goes in with the new homestead application, due March 1. The new homestead must be established within three years of the January 1 of the year you gave up the old one.

Watch renting if the house sits empty before the sale. Renting on January 1 loses the exemption, and renting for more than six months counts as abandonment. Changing the name on the deed can also remove a homestead, so review any transfer to an heir before you sign.

Condo sellers should ask the association about assessments before listing. If Florida's SB-4-D building safety law affects the condo market, the appraiser says it will value those properties accordingly and review the effect of assessment fees case by case.

Boca Raton, Boynton Beach and West Palm Beach charge a Fire Rescue Assessment on commercial property, based on use and square footage. For some properties it can exceed $10,000. If you own rental or small commercial property, get the county's figure before you agree on a price.

On a Palm Beach County deed the state's documentary stamp tax is 70 cents for every $100 of consideration. Everyone named on the deed is answerable for it. Ask the clerk whether any local housing surtax applies to your deed.

The clerk also adds page-based recording charges, and the deed needs two subscribing witnesses. Think your assessment is wrong? Phone the appraiser at 561.355.3230 and ask for an informal review. The next step is a petition to the Value Adjustment Board, filed through the county clerk.

sections.h2: Storm damage and missed mortgage payments
sections.html:
Storm damage reaches the tax bill the year after it happens, since values follow the condition of the home on January 1. A home that is uninhabitable for more than 30 days may qualify for a partial refund, and a rebuilt home that stays within 110 percent of the original square footage can keep its homestead after a calamity.

With a mortgage in default, a Florida court can order a public sale 20 to 35 days after judgment, and the bidder leaves a 5 percent deposit. Any surplus runs through the clerk. Talk to a Florida attorney or housing counselor early, so you know your choices before a sale date is set.

sections.h2: Timeline for a quick Boca Raton sale
sections.html:
A cash purchase can move fast, but only if the paperwork is ready. Start by pulling your parcel page and checking which exemptions sit on it. Next, order a payoff from each lender and ask the city about open permits. Then collect offers in writing and compare what each would leave you after recording charges, tax proration and any repairs you agree to make. Once you pick one, the title agent orders the search and prepares the deed. Signing happens before two witnesses, and the clerk records the deed afterward.

Condo and association properties add a step. Associations may have to approve the buyer or issue a statement of dues you owe. Make that request the day you decide to sell.

sections.h2: What to line up before closing
sections.html: Paperwork gaps cost sellers more time than price disputes do. Before you accept anything, make sure each owner on title can sign, then ask the title agent for a draft settlement statement. Read it line by line, since the deed tax, recording charges and any prorated tax bill all land there. When a buyer wants repairs, ask for the request in writing and decide what you will fix before the contract deadline.

faqs.q: Is Boca Raton in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: Yes. Property records come from the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser, and the county tax collector sends the bills.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Exemptions move with the owner, so the buyer files their own, and the sale resets assessed value to market on the next January 1.

faqs.q: What is the doc stamp rate on a Boca Raton deed?
faqs.a: It is 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Every party to the deed is liable to the state.

faqs.q: Can I rent out my Boca Raton house and keep homestead?
faqs.a: Only within limits. Short stays of 30 days or less in a year are allowed, but longer rentals risk the exemption, renting on January 1 loses it, and more than six months is abandonment.

faqs.q: How do I dispute a Boca Raton assessment?
faqs.a: Start with an informal review by calling the appraiser at 561.355.3230. If the issue remains, petition the Value Adjustment Board through the county clerk.
